definitions.explanation: A horizontal line drawn through text to indicate deletion or correction. Used in both handwritten documents and digital text formatting.

examples.japanese: {間違|まちが}えた{部分|ぶぶん}に{取|と}り{消|け}し{線|せん}を{引|ひ}いた。
examples.english: I drew a strikethrough line on the incorrect part.

examples.japanese: {取|と}り{消|け}し{線|せん}は{二重線|にじゅうせん}で{引|ひ}いてください。
examples.english: Please draw the deletion line as a double line.

examples.japanese: ワープロで{取|と}り{消|け}し{線|せん}の{書式|しょしき}を{設定|せってい}する{方法|ほうほう}を{教|おし}えてください。
examples.english: Please tell me how to set strikethrough formatting in the word processor.

notes:
In formal Japanese documents (especially official forms), mistakes are corrected by drawing a {二重線|にじゅうせん} (double line) through the error and stamping the correction with a personal seal ({訂正印|ていせいいん}). Simple erasure is not acceptable on official documents.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {取|と}り{消|け}し{線|せん}を{引|ひ}く — to draw a strikethrough
- {二重|にじゅう}{取|と}り{消|け}し{線|せん} — double strikethrough
- {取|と}り{消|け}し{線|せん}で{消|け}す — to cross out with a strikethrough

RELATED WORDS:
- {取|と}り{消|け}し — cancellation
- {訂正|ていせい} — correction
- {二重線|にじゅうせん} — double line
